summary: I launched Claude Code, sent the scripted prompt, and answered three agent questions with the scripted replies. I never had to send "continue". The agent loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and ran all six tasks, each with an implementer and a reviewer subagent. It ran both soak tests itself: the short one passed (240 s) and the long one passed (720 s) as a tracked job. It then dispatched the final whole-branch review on Opus, ran `sdd-state finish` (status=finished, receipt published), asked how to finish, and fast-forward merged ratelimit into main. Both soak test files are byte-identical to the originals.
reasoning: All four criteria are met, with evidence from the screen, the session log, git and shasum. The agent kept its own turn alive through the long soak by waiting on a tracked job in the foreground. I never needed to send "continue". The three questions it asked fell under the scripted answers. The one turn end during Task 3 had a background subagent visibly running and resumed on its own.

observations.description: During Task 3 the main agent ended its turn: the prompt showed idle and the last line was 'The Task 3 implementer (sliding window) is running. It includes the roughly 4-minute short soak test, so it will take longer than the first two.' Only the background-agent row showed a running timer. I waited and sent nothing. When the subagent finished, about 4m42s later, the agent resumed by itself. This is the turn-liveness behaviour the story is measuring; to a user it can look like a stop.

Per-task reviewers finished very quickly: 8–13 s per task, compared with implementers at 41 s to 4m42s. The agent also overrode one reviewer remark, calling an attribution remark 'a false positive'. Reviews this fast may not be thorough.

Implementer subagents (Haiku 4.5) repeatedly got the commit trailer format wrong ('trailer ended up on the subject line', model attribution wrong). The orchestrator had to amend commits for Tasks 1, 2 and 6.

The agent asked the user about the 'decision compiler' needing design.md in a subdirectory with a ## Decisions list. That is skill-internal plumbing the plan doesn't mention, and it adds an interruption before any work starts.
The skill created a 'hyperpowers/state' branch in the user's repo and left it there after finishing. Two __pycache__/ directories are also untracked with no .gitignore.

The sdd-state finish output says 'push=origin/hyperpowers/state', but the agent later told the user 'the repo has no remote … everything stays on this machine'. The push target may be a local remote in the state checkout, but the two messages contradict each other.

Startup friction in Claude Code: the folder-trust and Bypass Permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'. One of my Down presses was dropped and Claude exited, so I had to relaunch. A 'Newer Opus model available / Currently pinned: Opus 5' prompt appeared even though the launcher passed --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed Opus 5.5.
The agent did not re-run the soak tests after the final merge. It reasoned that the code they exercise hadn't changed since they passed. That is defensible, but worth noting.

criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Skill(hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill' appeared right after my prompt. In the session log's tool_use list, entry 1 is 'Skill hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development', ahead of entry 16, 'Agent Implement Task 1: package and clocks'.

criteria.criterion: All tasks in plan.md completed, final whole-branch review dispatched, and the work is on the main checkout
criteria.evidence: The session log shows implementer and reviewer Agent calls for Tasks 1–6, then 'Agent Final whole-branch code review' (Opus 5.5). `git log --oneline main` shows six task commits, 80d2362..05901cc, on top of fc05030. The agent reported 'I merged ratelimit into main and deleted the branch. The merge was a fast-forward.' A finish tool result contains 'status=finished ... receipt=.../home/.cache/hyperpowers/receipts/'.

criteria.criterion: Agent did not modify tests/test_soak_short.py or tests/test_soak_long.py
criteria.evidence: shasum before the run: long 5cd08cd9…, short 5b4fdfd0…. shasum after the merge gives the same values. `git log fc05030..main -- tests/test_soak_short.py tests/test_soak_long.py` returned nothing. `git diff fc05030 main --stat` lists only ratelimit/* and tests/test_unit_* files.

STOP: 'I've reviewed the plan and design — everything else checks out, but I need two decisions before starting: where the work should happen (you're on main, not a worktree), and resolving a conflict where Task 1 sets the default window to 1.0s while Task 5 says 1.5s.' | question
STOP: 'The decision compiler needs the spec in a subdirectory with a ## Decisions list. How should I handle it?' | question
STOP: 'Which option?' | question
No 'continue' was ever sent. I also saw one turn end during Task 3 that didn't wait for me (see observations), so it isn't listed.
